engine.meaning: Everything survives, nearly verbatim: "Preheat the oven to 425°F", "For an 8-inch frying pan this can be 25–30 minutes", "stored in the fridge for several days".
engine.sense: The swaps fit: "lunch or tea (supper)", "self-raising corn meal", "full-cream milk", "frying pan", "baking tin", "whack it in the oven".
engine.authenticity: Local words dropped into the original's clipped recipe prose: "If using cast-iron frying pan, whack it in the oven to heat." The vocabulary is right, but the voice stays American recipe-card.
engine.register: Largely untranslated: "Southern Cornbread is a hearty, unsweetened variety of cornbread, widely served in the Southeastern United States." Spelling and kitchen words localised, little else. Far under level 4.
engine.tone: The plain instructional tone is untouched.
engine.flow: Reads as the original; one jarring join where slang meets terse recipe grammar: "If using cast-iron frying pan, whack it in the oven to heat."
engine.variety: Barely any slang to vary; "frying pan" and "baking tin" repeat as the original's terms do.

yarn-troppo.meaning: Every step and quantity survives, plus metric: "425°F (220°C)", "8x8-inch (20x20 cm) baking tin". Additions hang off the text: "none of your cakey stuff" (on unsweetened), "Hard, I know." (on the cooling wait), "so don't stress" (on lumpy batter).
yarn-troppo.sense: Terms fit: "tea (supper, they call it)", "feed", "brekkie", "getting stuck into it", "whack it in the oven", "dish it up", "Crank the oven up".
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Mostly natural kitchen-yarn voice ("Righto, Southern Cornbread.", "unsweetened, mind"), with a stock tag bolted on: "Fair dinkum." and "here's the bit that gets ya".
yarn-troppo.register: Full level-4 voice, talked through from the first line: "Righto", "dead easy", "brekkie", "don't stress", "fair warning". No swearing, within vulgarity 1.
yarn-troppo.tone: Still a usable recipe, but the asides make it chattier than the original's neutral wiki tone: "Then leave it to cool for 5 minutes in the pan before you dish it up. Hard, I know."
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud well, with a little padding: "Don't preheat any other kind of frying pan or baking tin, just the cast iron.", "Go easy on it and don't overmix."
yarn-troppo.variety: Varied: "Righto", "mind", "dead easy", "feed", "getting stuck into it", "Crank", "whack", "pop", "dish it up", "fair warning".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably the recipe; the buttermilk curiosity is kept and played up: "And here's the bit that gets ya".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Everything survives, with metric added: "425°F (220°C)", "8x8-inch (20x20 cm) baking tin", "For an 8-inch frying pan that can be 25–30 minutes".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "tea (supper)", "dead easy", "feed", "brekkie", "tucking in", "whack it in the oven", "pop it in the oven", "tea towel".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Sounds like an Australian recipe written by a local: "It's dead easy to make and usually goes on the table as the bread with lunch or tea", "Go easy and don't overmix it."
yarn-dinkum.register: Level 4 in voice, though modest in slang density for a recipe: "dead easy", "feed", "brekkie", "whack", "pop". No swearing, within the dial. A touch light.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Keeps the plain, helpful recipe tone.
yarn-dinkum.flow: Smooth throughout: "Pour the batter into the pan and pop it in the oven."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Reasonable variety; "Go easy" and "wet through" fine, nothing leaned on, but not much range.
yarn-dinkum.essence: The recipe whole, with its buttermilk note.

dinkum-3.meaning: Steps and quantities survive with metric throughout. One shift: "Plenty of people over there will even make a quick, simple feed of it" turns "It is not unusual for some people to occasionally" into a stronger claim.
dinkum-3.sense: Terms fit: "tea (supper)", "feed", "brekkie", "tucking in", "Crank the oven up", "whack it", "a good squirt of spray oil".
dinkum-3.authenticity: Natural local voice: "Don't preheat any other sort of frying pan or baking tin, mind.", "The batter'll be a bit lumpy, and that's fine."
dinkum-3.register: Level 4 voice without overdoing it: "Crank", "whack", "mind", "feed", "brekkie". Within vulgarity 1.
dinkum-3.flow: Smooth: "If there's any cornbread left over, wrap it in a damp tea towel (keeps it moist) and it'll keep in the fridge for several days."

unharnessed.meaning: All steps and quantities survive. "(to stop it drying out)" and "a few days" for "several days" are close enough; nothing invented.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly apt: "frypan", "bung it in the oven", "feed", "brekkie", "getting stuck into it", "don't overmix the bugger". "knock together a quick, simple feed" fits.
unharnessed.authenticity: Mostly natural ("frypan" is the local word), but "a doddle" is British and "(tea, if you like)" reads oddly as a gloss on "dinner".
unharnessed.register: Full level 4 with a dad-level swear used naturally: "Go easy and don't overmix the bugger." Within vulgarity 1.
unharnessed.tone: Plain recipe tone kept; the "bugger" adds warmth without flippancy.
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Tip the batter into the frypan and whack it in the oven."
unharnessed.essence: The recipe whole, keeping "Procedure" and the buttermilk note.
